chapter: Guitar, recordings and Johnny St. Cyr
title: Recording with Johnny St. Cyr and playing solos
summary: Allen mentions St. Cyr's praise; Ernest recorded with him on Southland, including The Pearls, single-string solos, and he discusses strings.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I mentioned before, we started the tape that Johnny St. Cyr mentioned that he thought you had such a wonderful style on your solos and all, that if he ever had a band, he'd like to play the rhythm guitar himself and have you as a featured soloist on guitar.
Yeah, I recorded some records with him three or four years ago.
Oh, you did?
Uh-huh. My father was on records with us, too. Uh-huh.
Uh, what name was the band down there? Do you remember?
John-
John- John- John-
I don't know if they ever did bring those records?
Probably didn't come out. I'm not familiar with it. That's what I was trying to think. Uh-huh. Of course, Johnny St. Cyr made some for Southland record, Joe Merez.
Yes, who he was? Joe Merez?
It was for him. Uh-huh. But I don't think that group came out then. Probably not.
I don't remember everything about him or anything about him.
Yeah, maybe they'll issue him someday and bring him out. I'd like to hear.
Yeah, I would like to listen to him myself and get a hold of him.
I wanted to listen to you now, a number that you're going to do to hear the band playing. Now that was, uh, what was it? The Pearls? The Pearls, yeah.

The Pearls, you recorded the Pearls then on Southland. That was a Jolly Roll Martin number, huh? That's right. That's right. That's a good number. You play a solo in that then too, I suppose. Do you, uh, feature just single string solos or what style do you, uh, play or do you have any certain system to work out when you go to play a solo or mixing chords in?
Well, in that particular session I did. Nothing but a single string work, wasn't it? Yeah. Yeah.
Uh-huh. I was going to ask the kind of strings you use too. Some people use only nylon strings or, uh, do you use all metal strings?
No. Right now I'm using that, uh, chrome nickel.
Chrome nickel.
It's, uh, a foreign made of strings, a labella strings.
Uh-huh.

I think there's a, there's quite a few, uh, factories, manufacturing that, uh, chrome nickel. I think. Gibson has them, and, uh, Gretsch and Epiliform. Yeah. Most all of them have it now, you know. I mean, I've been using labella, chrome nickel. Uh-huh. Uh-huh.
